category_title: Students with ASD and learning difficulties who prioritize neatness over speed
minimal_context: The student is using a stylus to answer math sums in the x20 game on a Nintendo DS.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time to do the x20 math game on your Nintendo DS. Please begin answering the sums.

STUDENT: (Sits looking at the Nintendo DS screen without starting the activity, waiting to be told what to do.)

TUTOR: Go ahead and start writing your answers.

STUDENT: (Slowly and carefully writes the first answer with the stylus, taking a long time to ensure the numbers are perfectly neat.)

TUTOR: Okay, try the next math sum.

STUDENT: (Writes an incorrect answer, looks away from the screen, and then immediately restarts the entire x20 game from the beginning.)

options.A: Withhold attention from the student when she restarts the x20 game on the DS.
options.B: Engage in academic talk by explaining a math concept or modeling the DS activity.
options.C: Teach a replacement behavior for when the student answers a math sum incorrectly.
options.D: Provide a calculator for the student to confirm her answers on the math sums.
